entry.title: Org mode is the best OBTF
entry.content:
• This content is written to be lateral post to r/onebigtextfile and spark the idea to many.

I wrote about OBTF as Second Brain with Org mode a while back, but that post was mostly "here is my datetree workflow." This one is a direct response to obtf.ru, a site that makes the case for One Big Text File a lot sharper than I did, and argues it against FOMO fatigue I've felt myself.

OBTF in some sense is a lazy man's system to get things done. But if you feel more lazier to even think of it, I'd highly recommend to read https://obtf.ru/en website, since it helps me as well to stay motivated to achieve its purpose.

OBTF's philosophy pitch

Their whole argument boils down to a handful of lines:

Your entire life, notes, tasks, ideas, logs, in one text file. Just .txt.

The best productivity system is the one you actually use. And nothing is simpler than a text file.

Search beats categories

No vendor lock-in, speed, offline by default, permanence. All fair, and none of it is specific to a bare .txt file. It's specific to plain text. You make use of many tools to suite your needs instead of you learning and adapting to a system.

Some posts on OBTF found over internet:

  • Forum post on MacPowerUsers
  • https://mrshll.uk/posts/plain-text-planner/
  • https://jeffhuang.com/productivity_text_file/
  • https://mrdizzy.blog/blog/obtf/
  • https://beardystarstuff.net/posts/2024-04-17.html
  • https://whhone.com/posts/one-line-per-day-diary-in-org-mode/

Where Org gives you more

"Search beats categories" is true until the file gets big enough that search alone stops being enough, and at that point you want structure you can turn on when you need it, not structure forced on you from day one.

I still keep a datetree, Year > Month > Day > entry, which gives me OBTF's own "newest entries first, just append and go" model: 

* 2026
** 2026-10 October
*** 2026-10-07 Tuesday
**** <whatever I'm capturing>            :tag1:tag2:

The difference from a flat file is that I'm not stuck with chronology as the only axis. A few things I still reach for on top of the datetree:

  • org-sparse-tree (C-c /): narrow the whole tree down to just the headings matching a tag or property, without touching the file itself.
  • consult-org-heading / consult-line (from the consult package): fuzzy-jump straight to a heading or line, which is the actual "search beats categories" experience, just inside a structured file instead of a flat one.
  • org-ql: for queries that are more than a single tag match, closer to a real query language over my notes than regexp-over-a-text-file ever was.
  • #+select_tags: export just the headings carrying a given tag into a throwaway buffer, which behaves like a temporary, generated "file" scoped to one topic, without ever having to actually split the real file.
  • org-super-links: Package to backlink org headings to one another.
  • org-agenda: Best way to get organized and plan for time. Paired with note taking, the agenda interface is so powerful that even I've underused it mostly to just get stuff done.
  • Tags: More detail on the tagging convention I use (the l@=/=n@=/=p@ prefixes) is in OBTF as Second Brain with Org mode.

Conclude

These might sound very much tied to emacs, yes thats mostly true. Environment so perfect that it can be called a monolith of emacs. But alas, people have ported org mode inspired modes and packages to various other ecosystem.

  • orgmode.nvim: OG clone for neovim
  • org.nvim: New and AI assisted clone of complete org library
  • neorg: Future of organizing life in neovim
  • grove: Beautiful org mode first task/notes android app
  • orgzly-revived: Org in mobile at ease
  • orgro: Good org mode reader for android+IOS

PS: I use official Emacs on Android as well bringing the same environment on the phone (_;)

Ultimately only thing that is required with note taking or system is to always review, revise, repeat and process them.

entry.title: OBTF as Second Brain with Org mode
entry.content:
One Big Text File is simply writing down mostly everything in single file to organize or manage data. This single file acts as the source of knowledge and holds all notes.

Second brain has been a buzz word, thanks to the sourcing of Zettelkasten method, every productivity freak is on the stance to organize their life and get things done.

But I soon came to the conclusion by reading many blogs and reddit discussions that, searching is far superior than organizing. On internet all we do is search for information, and not organize or build system just to get info. This is how note taking should work as well. Just for efficient retrieval and storage.

Thanks to my introduction to emacs and getting deep into rabbit hole, Org mode has been the great tool to handle plain text file as an Organization platform. Just like emacs (OS), Org mode can also be extended to endless limit (I dare say it). If emacs is OS, Org mode is for me Init system (systemd).

You can read more about my note taking journey in Wrap up on my Bioinformatics Masters Journey.

This context is also written in favor to post it on r/obtf

Org mode is the best tool for managing OBTF

Many popular workflow would go by simple format as bullet points with Time date and info, and regexp based searching via CLI (rg, vim, grep, sed…. bash scripts)

Org mode has many bells and whistles (features) that aid in this method. Tags, integration with commands and rich source of documentation (one of the best things of Emacs or org mode). Thanks to emacs and protesilaos stavrou I learnt how important are documentation and writing sensible notes. It means alot for future self to recognize and re-instantiate the thoughts and state.

Org mode has an datetree method which has file heading hierarchy in the Year > Month > Day and 4th nested heading follows any notes. 

* 2022
** 2022-10 October
*** 2022-10-07 Friday
*** 2022-10-08 Saturday
**** <Any notes I'm capturing>            :tag1:tag2:

This gives out the leverage of journaling, but also a lazy man's organization. I use tagging extensively to most of the (4th) heading based on context so as to narrow down to filter. 

# learning notes --- l@
#+tags: l@coding l@emacs l@bioinfo l@nix l@bash l@julia l@rstats l@python l@devnote l@latex l@til

# generic notes to remember or readme --- n@
#+tags: n@linux n@shell n@cli n@book n@idea

# projects --- p@
#+tags: p@webcli p@cyanate p@scitomep
  • These tag help to categorize the heading in some (lazy) way

Org mode has org-sparse-tree bound to C-c / which helps to narrow down based on tag or property. Also another emacs package consult helps to take it up further via consult-line and consult-org-heading along with org-ql package. Org mode also has #+select_tags to export headings to file. 

#+select_tags: r@book

With that we can C-c C-e (org-export-dispatch) and press "O O" (make sure org is in org-export-backends) to get temporary Org buffer only with those heading. This logically acts as an individual file with that tag/category, thus being atomic in my sense. Org-sparse-tree might also be same.

-—

Key takeaways

whatever the system or the tool is, the main takeaways every resource provides is to review the notes and write it for future self. Every capture is to review back and make the fleeting note into and rich information. This OBTF with org mode satisfies that needs given that user reviews the notes and visits back to digest it again.
